chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ismail ibn Umar, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed for the womb there are four pathways; whichever pathway the fluid travels through, from it can come one child, and two, and three, and four; and to one pathway there cannot be more than one (at a time).

key_terms.الرحم: The womb/uterus (anatomical term used in the context of reproduction)
key_terms.الماء: The fluid/water; in this biological context it refers to the male reproductive fluid (semen/seed)
key_terms.الولد: The child or offspring; the product of conception
key_terms.سبل: Pathways or passages (singular: سبيل); here referring to the anatomical channels of the womb

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the maximum number of children from one womb passage?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides an anatomical teaching about the structure of the womb, stating it has four pathways through which the reproductive fluid may travel, with each pathway capable of producing offspring — one, two, three, or four — but no single pathway can yield more than one child simultaneously. This hadith is situated within a broader jurisprudential discussion about the maximum number of children a woman can bear in one delivery, with implications for matters such as parentage confirmation and inheritance rulings in Islamic law.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from someone else, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Ismail Bin Umar, from Shuayb Al Aqarquqy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘For womb there are four ways in whichever way the water (seed) travels. There can be from it the one child, and two, and three, and four, and there cannot happen to a way (out), for more than one (at a time)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya and others have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from ’Isma‘il ibn ‘Umar from Shu’ayb al-‘Aqarqufiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

The womb has four ways in whichever way the seed (water) finds the path thereof comes a child, one child, two children , three children or four children . In (through) one way only one child can come and no more/”
